calls.title: Website Sync
calls.summary: The team discussed finalizing the design direction for the website, emphasizing solid colors and a clean aesthetic to cater to preferences expressed by key stakeholders. They acknowledged significant gaps in current content and committed to a comprehensive rewrite to enhance user engagement and clarity. A launch target of April 1 was set for the updated site, prioritizing core product pages for maximum impact. To streamline the design process, a modular template strategy was proposed, allowing for unique elements while maintaining efficiency. The need for improved collaboration and structured feedback loops was recognized to facilitate better project tracking and coordination among teams. Automation of asset creation was highlighted as a priority to enhance marketing efficiency and maintain visual consistency across materials.
calls.keywords: Website Design, Content Strategy, User Experience, Product Pages, Marketing Assets, Interactive Elements

## Summary
Website direction remains pending Ashley’s meeting, with no immediate rush. The team will prioritize performance work first, using it as a starting point and giving Yousef process exposure. Website bugs and enhancements should be consolidated and tracked in the Notion board, while Chris assesses effort and priority and assigns contributors. Ready requests can reach Yousef through the board, Slack descriptions, or Loom, although reducing informal Slack bypasses is preferred. Performance improvements may reduce CMS collections and make marketing needs more self-service. Jack is managing three projects, completed Rippling work today, and is finishing DEI training; follow-up is planned after Ashley’s discussion. Benefits enrollment was reviewed twice for November open enrollment and plan changes. Aetna provider coverage was confirmed with no provider changes expected. Opolis group coverage was recommended for the freelancer community, while its S-Corp requirement, payroll administration fee, and eligibility restrictions were noted. Potential savings and tax advantages may exceed fees, and Aetna was considered the best solo-plan option.
